response.headline: EU court adviser rejects Meta's fight against EU antitrust demands for Facebook data
response.summary: An adviser to Europe's top court on Thursday backed ‌Meta Platforms' fight against EU antitrust ‌regulators over what the U.S. tech giant said were ​aberrant requests for information from the later during two investigations into the company.  Meta had taken its case to the Luxembourg-based Court of ‌Justice of the ⁠European Union, questioning EU demands related to its Facebook social network ⁠and online classified ads.  "In his opinion, Advocate General Athanasios Rantos proposes that the Court of ​Justice dismiss ​both appeals and ​uphold the judgments ‌of the General Court", the court said in a statement, adding that Rantos said in his non-binding opinion that the General Court "did not err in law in assessing the ‌necessity of the information ​requested or in examining the ​safeguards for ​its provision."
